title: Microsoft Purview: auto-labeling ceiling for SharePoint and OneDrive rises to 500,000 files a day (Worldwide)
summary: Hold: the licensing paragraph carries client-side entitlements over to service-side auto-labeling, including an unconfirmed standalone P2 entitlement. The rollout, automatic application to active policies, throughput caveat and documented control paths are supported.

claims.where: title; summary; What's changing; rationale: risk
claims.claim: The maximum SharePoint and OneDrive auto-labeling capacity rises from 100,000 to up to 500,000 files per tenant per day.
claims.quote: We are increasing the maximum auto-labeling capacity for SharePoint and OneDrive from 100,000 up to 500,000 files per tenant per day.

claims.claim: The roadmap presents the increase as closing labeling gaps and helping prepare data for Microsoft 365 Copilot.
claims.quote: With sensitivity labels and protection settings applied to more files sooner, organizations can better prepare their data estate for Microsoft 365 Copilot with greater confidence.

claims.claim: Roadmap item 571309 describes the same increase for GCC, GCC High and DoD.
claims.quote: "id": 571309; "clouds": ["GCC", "GCC High", "DoD"]; "description": "We are increasing the maximum auto-labeling capacity for SharePoint and OneDrive from 100,000 up to 500,000 files per tenant per day."

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment; Governance guidance; rationale: impact
claims.claim: Microsoft expects no end-user experience changes.
claims.quote: No end-user experience changes are expected.

claims.claim: For organisations not using auto-labeling, Microsoft recommends creating a SharePoint or OneDrive policy in simulation mode.
claims.quote: If you are not currently using auto-labeling, we recommend: ... Create an auto-labeling policy for SharePoint or OneDrive in simulation mode.

claims.claim: Microsoft recommends reviewing simulation results to validate expected outcomes.
claims.quote: Review simulation results to validate expected labeling outcomes.

claims.claim: Microsoft recommends enabling the policy after validation.
claims.quote: Enable the policy after validation to take advantage of the increased daily processing limit.

claims.claim: This update introduces no new labeling conditions.
claims.quote: This update does not introduce new labeling conditions, data storage locations, or protection capabilities.

claims.claim: Auto-labeling policies are service-side labeling of stored SharePoint and OneDrive files based on administrator-defined conditions.
claims.quote: Service-side labeling when content is already saved (in SharePoint or OneDrive) or emailed (processed by Exchange Online): Use an auto-labeling policy.

claims.where: What's changing; Governance controls; rationale: risk
claims.claim: The 500,000-file daily maximum is tenant-wide in aggregate across all auto-labeling policies.
claims.quote: The absolute maximum throughput is 500,000 automatically labeled SharePoint and OneDrive files per tenant per day, in aggregate across all auto-labeling policies.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment; Governance guidance; Open questions
claims.claim: The ceiling is not a guaranteed or consistently expected daily rate and actual throughput can be lower.
claims.quote: This ceiling isn't a guaranteed or consistently expected daily processing rate; actual throughput can be lower.

claims.claim: Learn says auto-labeling policies run continuously until deleted.
claims.quote: Auto-labeling policies run continuously until they're deleted.

claims.claim: New and modified files are included using the current policy settings.
claims.quote: For example, new and modified files will be included with the current policy settings.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure; Governance guidance: Before rollout
claims.claim: A label applying encryption in a SharePoint or OneDrive auto-labeling policy must use Assign permissions now.
claims.quote: When the auto-labeling policy includes locations for SharePoint or OneDrive, the label must be configured for the Assign permissions now setting

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure; Governance guidance: Before rollout
claims.claim: Those encryption labels must have User access to content expires set to Never.
claims.quote: User access to content expires must be set to Never.

claims.claim: Label encryption restricts reading to people authorised by its encryption settings.
claims.quote: Can be decrypted only by users authorized by the label's encryption settings.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Security & identity; Why it matters
claims.claim: An auto-labeling policy can be configured to override a lower-priority manually applied label.
claims.quote: For auto-labeling policies that apply a sensitivity label, you can select a setting to override a manually applied label that has lower priority.

claims.claim: A policy configured to remove a label can remove the selected label even when it was manually applied.
claims.quote: An auto-labeling policy configured to automatically remove a label can remove the selected label, including when the label was manually applied, and leave the content unlabeled.

claims.where: controls[1].note; Risk assessment; Governance guidance; Governance controls: Roles
claims.claim: Turning a policy from Ready to turn on to On requires Compliance Administrator or Compliance Data Administrator.
claims.quote: Turning a policy from Ready to turn on to On requires Compliance Administrator or Compliance Data Administrator.

claims.claim: Service-side auto-labeling operates without user interaction.
claims.quote: Because the user doesn't interact with the labeling process, auto-labeling policies don't support recommended labeling

claims.claim: A policy must run at least one simulation before automatically applying or removing labels.
claims.quote: You can't automatically label documents and emails, or remove labels, until your policy has run at least one simulation.

claims.claim: Simulation is the only documented pre-enforcement checkpoint in the auto-labeling workflow.
claims.quote: Searched: Purview auto-labeling simulation only checkpoint approval before enable policies no active policy scale increase. Read apply-sensitivity-label-automatically simulation workflow and troubleshoot-auto-labeling-policies search excerpts; no separate approval gate found.

claims.claim: Open files cannot be auto-labeled.
claims.quote: Files can't be auto-labeled if they're part of an open session (the file is open).

claims.claim: PDFs are skipped unless PDF labeling is enabled for the tenant.
claims.quote: If PDF labeling isn't enabled, PDFs are skipped entirely: PDFs aren't evaluated or sent for labeling, and no label is applied.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Change & support; Governance guidance: After rollout
claims.claim: Policy labeling progress figures refresh every 48 hours.
claims.quote: This progress information updates every 48 hours, so you can expect to see the most current data about every other day.

claims.claim: The capability is included in qualifying licenses rather than separately entitled by the ceiling increase.
claims.quote: | Client and service-side automatic sensitivity labeling | Included | Included |

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing
claims.claim: Standalone Azure Information Protection Premium P2, or a P2-tier add-on to E3 or Business Premium, establishes entitlement to this service-side feature.
claims.quote: Searched: "service-side" "Azure Information Protection Premium P2" auto-labeling licensing. Read the auto-labeling surface table, Purview service-side SKU matrix and AIP service-description excerpt; P2's client-side or generic automatic-classification entries do not establish this entitlement.
claims.fix: Remove Azure Information Protection Premium P2 from the service-side SKU list and replace 'requires an E5 or P2-tier add-on' with 'requires an eligible subscription or add-on for service-side automatic sensitivity labeling; check the Client and service-side automatic sensitivity labeling matrix.' Link https://learn.microsoft.com/office365/servicedescriptions/microsoft-365-service-descriptions/microsoft-365-tenantlevel-services-licensing-guidance/microsoft-purview-service-description#microsoft-purview-information-protection-sensitivity-labeling.

claims.claim: E3 or Business Premium manual-labeling entitlement does not include automatic labeling.
claims.quote: You have E3 or Business Premium. Manual labeling entitlement doesn't include automatic labeling. Check the feature matrix for an eligible subscription or add-on for the labeling method you intend to use.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing; rationale: cost
claims.claim: No separate charge, meter or license specific to the higher daily ceiling is documented.
claims.quote: Searched: Purview auto-labeling 500000 ceiling additional charge license meter pricing. Read apply-sensitivity-label-automatically, Purview service description, purview-billing-models, the roadmap and MC1461154; no ceiling-specific charge, meter or license found.

claims.where: Cost and licensing; Governance controls: Roles
claims.claim: Viewing file contents in simulation source view requires Data Classification Content Viewer.
claims.quote: To view file or email contents in the source view, you must have the Data Classification Content Viewer role

claims.claim: Global admins do not have Data Classification Content Viewer by default.
claims.quote: Global admins don't have this role by default.

claims.claim: Supported file formats include PDF and Word, Excel and PowerPoint files.
claims.quote: PDF documents and Office files for Word (.docx), PowerPoint (.pptx), and Excel (.xlsx) are supported.

claims.claim: A OneDrive account not associated with its corresponding user account is unsupported.
claims.quote: A OneDrive account that isn't associated with its user account (sometimes called a detached OneDrive account) isn't supported for auto-labeling or simulation.

claims.claim: Sensitivity labels must be enabled for Office files in SharePoint and OneDrive.
claims.quote: Sensitivity labels are enabled for Office files in SharePoint and OneDrive. Required before any label can be applied to files in those locations.

claims.claim: There is a maximum of 100 auto-labeling policies per tenant.
claims.quote: Maximum of 100 auto-labeling policies per tenant.

claims.claim: The Auto-labeling page is not visible in unsupported regions because of a backend Azure dependency.
claims.quote: Auto-labeling isn't currently available in all regions because of a backend Azure dependency. If your tenant can't support this functionality, the Auto-labeling page isn't visible in the Microsoft Purview portal.

claims.claim: The portal limit is 1,000 explicitly included or excluded SharePoint sites per policy.
claims.quote: In the portal, each policy can target up to 1,000 explicitly included or excluded SharePoint sites

claims.claim: Keeping the default All selection is exempt from the explicit-location maximums.
claims.quote: If you keep the default configuration of All, this configuration is exempt from these maximums.

claims.claim: Set-AutoSensitivityLabelPolicy runs in Security & Compliance PowerShell.
claims.quote: This cmdlet is available only in Security & Compliance PowerShell.

claims.claim: The AddOneDriveLocation parameter adds OneDrive locations to the policy.
claims.quote: The AddOneDriveLocation parameter specifies the OneDrive sites to add to the list of included sites when you aren't using the value All for the OneDriveLocation parameter. You identify the site by its URL value.

claims.claim: Mode TestWithoutNotifications is test mode without policy actions or notifications.
claims.quote: TestWithoutNotifications: An audit mode where no actions are taken, and no notifications are sent (Test mode).

claims.claim: Mode Disable disables the policy.
claims.quote: Disable: The policy is disabled.

claims.claim: Policy locations can be edited through Purview > Solutions > Information Protection > Policies > Auto-labeling policies > policy > Edit policy > Choose locations where you want to apply the label.
claims.quote: Solutions > Information Protection > Policies > Auto-labeling policies. ... For a policy in the Off section, select the Edit policy button. ... Choose locations where you want to apply the label

claims.claim: Set-AutoSensitivityLabelPolicy -Identity <PolicyIdParameter> -AddSharePointLocation <SharePointSites> modifies the policy's included SharePoint sites.
claims.quote: The AddSharePointLocation parameter specifies the SharePoint sites to add to the list of included sites when you aren't using the value All for the SharePointLocation parameter. You identify the site by its URL value.

claims.claim: Turning auditing on or off requires the Audit Logs role in Exchange Online.

claims.claim: Microsoft 365 auditing must be on for auto-labeling simulation.
claims.quote: Auditing is turned on for Microsoft 365. Required for simulation.

claims.claim: The Activity explorer export cmdlet runs in Security & Compliance PowerShell.
claims.quote: This cmdlet is available only in Security & Compliance PowerShell.

claims.claim: Activity explorer export requires assigned permissions in Security & Compliance PowerShell.

claims.claim: Activity explorer reports on up to 30 days of data.

claims.quote: Simulation mode supports up to 20,000,000 matched files. ... This maximum of 20,000,000 matched files applies to simulation mode only and not to an auto-labeling policy that's already turned on

claims.claim: Nothing is documented about this scale update changing a tenant with no auto-labeling policies.
claims.quote: Searched: "500,000" "auto-labeling" "no" "policies". Read auto-labeling guidance, MC1461154 and the roadmap; the increase applies to existing policies and the notice recommends policy creation for nonusers, not automatic creation by this update.

claims.claim: Per-policy review pages expose Labeled items and Labeling failures, including failure reasons worth reviewing even at low failure volumes.
claims.quote: Use Labeled items to review successfully labeled files. Use Labeling failures ... to investigate failures. Select a file and review its failure reason. ... Review the failure reason even when few files fail.
